$comment: Provenance record for the design content pack. Method: every file in the pack was byte-compared (md5) against the candidate upstream repositories named in runtime/agents/design-engineer.md, fetched from GitHub raw at the shas recorded under `sources`. Licenses were read from the upstream LICENSE files themselves (copied verbatim into packs/design/licenses/), not inferred from a README or from memory. HONESTY RULE: `provenance` is `verified` only when a byte-level or field-level comparison against a named upstream succeeded during this audit; `asserted` when the origin is documented in-repo but was not independently confirmed; `unknown` when neither holds. A license is never recorded unless it was read from an upstream LICENSE file or declared in the vendored file's own frontmatter. Where the audit could not establish something — most importantly the commit each subtree was originally vendored at — the field is null with a `nullReason`, rather than guessed. Paths are relative to xx-stack/packs/design/.

audit.method: md5 byte-comparison of every pack file against upstream raw.githubusercontent.com content, plus frontmatter field survey
audit.tooling: curl + md5sum; GitHub trees API for upstream layout
audit.limitation: Comparison is against each upstream's current default branch, not against the tree as it stood when this pack was vendored. Files recorded as `modified` may differ because of local edits, upstream drift since vendoring, or both; where the audit inspected the diff, the cause is stated.

sources.licenseEvidence: LICENSE at repo root, fetched 2026-08-03 and copied verbatim to licenses/nexu-io-open-design-Apache-2.0.txt
sources.nullReason: The vendoring commit was never recorded. The pack entered this repo in local commit fb93297 (later restructured by d458c02) with no upstream sha noted. Recovering it would require bisecting upstream history against our file hashes; it was not attempted.
sources.notice: Apache-2.0 section 4(b) requires modified files to carry a notice of modification. This manifest is that notice: see the `modifiedFiles` lists below for the exact set.

sources.licenseEvidence: Two independent confirmations: LICENSE at repo root (fetched 2026-08-03, copied verbatim), and `license: MIT` declared in the frontmatter of all 57 vendored SKILL.md files.
sources.nullReason: Not recorded at vendoring time. The snapshot is datable only relatively: it contains 57 of the 67 skills upstream now publishes, including 7 slugs upstream has since dropped or renamed.

sources.licenseEvidence: LICENSE at repo root, fetched 2026-08-03 and copied verbatim to licenses/voltagent-awesome-design-md-MIT.txt
sources.nullReason: Only one file in this pack traces to this upstream, so the repo head was not pinned.
sources.scopeNote: runtime/agents/design-engineer.md names this repo as a source for the whole design pack. The audit found exactly one file that actually comes from it (design-systems/bmw-m/DESIGN.md). The agent frontmatter overstates this upstream's contribution.

sources.licenseEvidence: LICENSE at repo root, read from a filtered clone on 2026-08-03 and copied verbatim (blob b31ddffd7a087dcdf4d780019f9b6b8c6db7f7b1, byte-identical). Shipped as a separate file from licenses/nexu-io-open-design-Apache-2.0.txt even though both are Apache-2.0: the two renderings differ in line-wrapping, in the §4 and §9 heading wording, and in the appendix copyright line, so neither was assumed to stand in for the other.
sources.nullReason: No file from this upstream is redistributed here. It contributes rule VALUES only, to craft/anti-ai-slop-rules.json, from plugins/stitch-utilities/skills/taste-design/SKILL.md.
sources.supplies: Seven of the 18 rules in craft/anti-ai-slop-rules.json, each tagged `source: stitch-skills`, plus three extra invented-metric phrasings folded into open-design's rule (the 18th, tagged `open-design + stitch-skills`). Eight further rules of its own were explicitly refused; see that file's `notAdopted` list, which records the reason for each.
sources.selfContainedNote: The skill's design guidance needs no hosted service. It lists Google Stitch and an optional Stitch MCP server under Prerequisites for its own generate-a-DESIGN.md workflow; none of the rules taken depend on either, and that workflow was not taken.
sources.conflictNote: This upstream and open-design disagree on one point and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over: stitch-skills recommends picsum.photos as a placeholder image host, open-design bans it. open-design's position holds here, because this pack's artifacts are self-contained single files and any runtime host fetch is what the gate exists to catch.

sources.licenseEvidence: LICENSE at repo root, read from a filtered clone on 2026-08-03 and copied verbatim to licenses/referodesign-refero_skill-MIT.txt (blob 2c7d699d6123a4dc9ea5ec7dfbc2939963e6ef01, byte-identical). NOTE: nexu-io/open-design attributes craft/ to '© Refero Design'; the LICENSE file itself says 'Copyright (c) 2026 Refero'. The shorter form is what the license text actually holds and is what is recorded here.
sources.nullReason: Nothing in this pack is vendored from refero_skill directly. It reaches us only as the second hop of a chain: nexu-io/open-design authored craft/ as an adaptation of refero_skill's references/, and we vendor open-design's files. No refero_skill file is redistributed here.
sources.relationshipEvidence: Verified, not taken on trust. (1) craft/README.md § Attribution states the adaptation and names the repo and license. (2) Three craft files — typography.md, color.md, anti-ai-slop.md — carry an inline '> Adapted from [refero_skill] (MIT)' blockquote. (3) refero_skill ships references/{typography,color,anti-ai-slop,motion,icons,copywriting,craft-details}.md, the same subject axis, at the same paths-by-topic. (4) Diffing refero's references/{anti-ai-slop,color,typography}.md against open-design's craft/ counterparts shows a heavy rewrite and condensation (378, 649, 827 diff lines respectively), not a copy — open-design's own copyright in the derived text is substantial. The chain is real; the bytes we hold are open-design's.
sources.scopeNote: The other eight craft rulebooks (typography-hierarchy, typography-hierarchy-editorial, state-coverage, animation-discipline, accessibility-baseline, rtl-and-bidi, form-validation, laws-of-ux) carry NO refero attribution, inline or in the README's file table, and postdate the three that do. They read as open-design's own work under Apache-2.0. The README's blanket 'craft content is adapted from refero_skill' is broader than the per-file evidence supports; both licenses are shipped, so the conservative reading costs nothing.

sources.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file shipped inside the skill directory, matching the file upstream ships at nexu-io/open-design design-templates/guizang-ppt/LICENSE. Preserved here byte-for-byte; do not edit or delete it.
sources.nullReason: No standalone upstream repository was identified for this author's template; it reaches us through nexu-io/open-design, which redistributes it under the author's own MIT terms rather than the repo-wide Apache-2.0.

subtrees.nature: vendored, with local modifications to 8 files (7 further files differ only because upstream moved on)

detail.modificationCause: Two causes, both observed in sampled diffs. (1) Local de-branding, applied by commit d458c02 'Restructure into three top-level components; dedupe, de-brand, fix CI' — e.g. design-systems/voltagent replaces 'GitHub stars badge' with 'community badge'. (2) Upstream drift since vendoring — e.g. design-systems/arc gained a '## 7. Usage Guardrails' section upstream that this copy predates.

exceptions.note: Byte-identical to VoltAgent/awesome-design-md design-md/bmw-m/DESIGN.md except for one line: upstream `name: BMW-M-design-analysis` was changed to `name: BMW M`. This is the only file in design-systems/ with YAML frontmatter, and the only one that does not come from open-design; open-design ships its own, different bmw-m.

detail.separationMethod: Separated by matching every file against upstream history with a blob:none clone: files whose content matches SOME historical upstream state are upstream drift; files matching NO upstream state at any commit are our edits. Before this, the two causes could not be told apart and all 15 were recorded as modified.

subtrees.copyrightNote: The content is written as 'Design System Inspired by <brand>' — prose analysis of publicly observable visual language, not copied brand assets. That framing is upstream's, authored at nexu-io/open-design and VoltAgent/awesome-design-md; it was NOT clean-room reinterpretation performed in this repo. Everything here is a redistributed copy of upstream text. Brand names, wordmarks, and trademarks referenced in the prose remain the property of their respective owners and are used nominatively.
subtrees.correctionNote: An earlier internal description of this pack characterised design-systems/ as clean-room reinterpretation authored here. That is wrong: 121 of 137 files are byte-identical to upstream. The correct characterisation is redistribution under Apache-2.0 (and MIT for bmw-m).

subtrees.nature: vendored verbatim (directory renamed from upstream `skills/` to `design-skills/`)

divergent.reason: Upstream rewrote this skill after our snapshot (different description, palette, and typography). Ours is the older upstream text, not a local edit.

absentFromUpstreamHead.reason: Present in this snapshot and in the snapshot-era upstream index, absent from bergside/awesome-design-skills at f631a09. Upstream appears to have dropped or renamed them. Their SKILL.md frontmatter carries the same `license: MIT` / `metadata.author: typeui.sh` declaration as the other 50, so the license is still established per-file even though the upstream path no longer resolves.

detail.inFileAttribution: All 57 SKILL.md files declare `license: MIT` and `metadata.author: typeui.sh` in frontmatter, and wrap their body in `<!-- TYPEUI_SH_MANAGED_START -->` markers. typeui.sh is the CLI that publishes the registry; Bergside is the copyright holder named in the upstream LICENSE.
detail.upstreamSize: 67 skills at f631a09; this pack vendors 57 of them.

removedFiles.reason: All 114 of its paths were broken: every entry declared `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` and `skills/<slug>/DESIGN.md`, but this pack renamed the directory to `design-skills/` and never applied the rename. Nothing read it — scripts/generate-design-catalog.mjs explicitly filtered it out. Verified before removal that it carried no information the directory tree does not: `slug` equals the directory name for all 57 entries, `name` equals the `name` field in the corresponding DESIGN.md frontmatter for all 57 entries (zero mismatches), and both paths are derivable from the slug. Fixing the paths would have made it correct but still unread, and would have broken byte-comparison against upstream — the one thing the file was actually good for. Its snapshot value is preserved above under `absentFromUpstreamHead` and `upstreamSize`.

subtrees.nature: part vendored, part authored here. 88 of 167 files are vendored SKILL.md/example.html from upstream (6 with local edits); the other 79 have no upstream counterpart at any path or commit and were written here.
subtrees.license: Apache-2.0, except workflow-skills/guizang-ppt/ which is MIT

detail.modificationCause: Sampled diffs are small and of two kinds: local pruning of upstream fields not used here (e.g. simple-deck drops upstream's `en_name`/`zh_name` bilingual frontmatter; blog-post drops upstream's `craft.requires` list and adds `featured: 11`), and upstream drift since vendoring. No skill was substantially rewritten.
detail.inFileAttribution: All 31 SKILL.md files retain upstream's `od:` frontmatter block — open-design's own metadata namespace — which is what identifies the subtree's origin from inside the files.
detail.documentedInRepo: workflow-skills/replit-deck/SKILL.md § 'Scope & provenance' names nexu-io/open-design as the issue tracker for this content and records its own snapshot date (2026-04-29, colors sampled from replit.com/slides with ImageMagick).
detail.authoredHereFiles: every references/checklist.md (31), references/layouts.md (31), and assets/template.html (31), plus quality-gates.json — upstream ships only SKILL.md + example.html per template
detail.authoredHereEvidence: No upstream counterpart exists at any path in any commit, and the checklists cite this repo's own design-prototype skill and its P0/P1/P2 severity vocabulary.

exceptions.note: Upstream open-design also ships a per-directory LICENSE for this template, confirming it is carved out of the repo-wide Apache-2.0. Our copy is preserved byte-for-byte. This is the only LICENSE file that existed anywhere in the design pack before this audit.

locallyAuthored.reason: References xx-stack-relative paths (packs/design/workflow-skills/...) and this repo's gate vocabulary; no counterpart at the upstream path. Authored here, covered by the repo root MIT LICENSE.

subtrees.contents: 11 brand-agnostic craft rulebooks + upstream's README.md and FUTURE_SECTIONS.md, vendored byte-for-byte; plus two files authored here (XX-STACK-NOTES.md, anti-ai-slop-rules.json)
subtrees.nature: vendored verbatim, zero local edits to any vendored file
subtrees.license: Apache-2.0 (nexu-io/open-design), over a two-hop chain from referodesign/refero_skill (MIT)
subtrees.axis: A fourth content axis for this pack, and the one genuinely new KIND of content. design-systems/ says what a brand looks like; design-skills/ supplies aesthetic direction; workflow-skills/ says how to build one artifact type; craft/ supplies the universal rules that hold regardless of brand (ALL CAPS needs >=0.06em tracking; cap visible accent uses at ~2 per screen; every stateful surface needs empty/loading/error/partial states).

detail.method: --filter=blob:none clone, `git archive HEAD craft`, then `git hash-object` on every landed file compared against `git rev-parse HEAD:craft/<file>`. All 13 vendored files verified byte-identical.
detail.tokenEstimateMethod: bytes/4 rounded, same convention as packs/rules/manifest.json

files.license: MIT structure; rule VALUES from two Apache-2.0 upstreams (nexu-io/open-design and google-labs-code/stitch-skills) — see its own `attribution` block, and every rule's `source` field

detail.whyReadmeWasNotRewritten: Task 30 proposed rewriting upstream's README for our paths. It was vendored unmodified instead: byte-comparability against upstream is the reason packs/ is .prettierignore'd, and editing the one file that documents the axis would forfeit it for the file most likely to drift. The corrections a reader needs — `pnpm lint:craft` is `scripts/check-craft-references.mjs` here, there is no daemon prompt-composer, `data-od-id` is an upstream desktop-app concern — are in craft/XX-STACK-NOTES.md, which is clearly ours.

optIn.mechanism: od.craft.requires in each workflow skill's SKILL.md frontmatter — upstream's own convention, inside the `od:` namespace block our 31 SKILL.md files already carry.
optIn.conventionEvidence: Not invented here. workflow-skills/saas-landing/SKILL.md already shipped `craft: requires: [typography, color, anti-ai-slop]` — the May-era upstream binding, carried in when the pack was vendored. This audit's earlier finding that blog-post 'drops upstream's craft.requires list' is the same signal from the other direction.
optIn.bindingProvenance: Every binding above is upstream's at dceac12, for the same slug, transcribed unchanged. saas-landing's pre-existing list gained `laws-of-ux` to match. The 19 unbound skills have no upstream binding and were left unbound rather than guessed — absence is a decision here, the way packs/rules/coverage.json records explicit empty entries. Note these bindings are resolved against SKILL.md bodies roughly three months behind upstream; taking the binding line without the rest of the drift is deliberate.
optIn.resolution: Selection is a budget decision against the target lane's context window, surfaced in the agent's reasoning. Nothing in the MCP server injects craft sections — the same position packs/rules takes with nano/mini/full.
optIn.check: scripts/check-craft-references.mjs asserts every slug named by an od.craft.requires resolves to craft/<slug>.md or appears in craft/FUTURE_SECTIONS.md. Upstream's contract, reimplemented (their `pnpm lint:craft` assumes a pnpm monorepo). NOT yet wired into `npm run verify` — that needs a package.json edit outside this change's scope.

detail.shelfWare: None. All 11 shipped sections are required by at least one skill, including laws-of-ux (5 skills) and form-validation (1), which Task 30 flagged as candidates to skip if unrequired.

subtrees.honestyNote: craft/ is not entirely new since we vendored. Three rulebooks (typography, color, anti-ai-slop) plus README.md landed upstream in 1edab99 on 2026-05-02T11:00+08:00 — about twelve hours BEFORE our vendoring window (9ee2c19 .. 483e00d) opened. They were available and we simply did not take them. The other eight landed 2026-05-05 through 2026-06-14, after the window closed, and are genuinely new: they are ~90% of the bytes. Recorded so the pack's record distinguishes what upstream added later from what we missed.
subtrees.copyrightNote: Brand-agnostic by construction — no brand names, no trademarks, no copied assets. The redistribution obligation is Apache-2.0's alone (license text shipped at licenses/nexu-io-open-design-Apache-2.0.txt); the MIT text for refero_skill is shipped as well because upstream declares the chain, even though no refero_skill file is redistributed here.
subtrees.ruleTableNote: craft/anti-ai-slop-rules.json is authored here and is the only file in this subtree that draws on a second upstream. It encodes 18 mechanically checkable rules — 10 from nexu-io/open-design, 7 from google-labs-code/stitch-skills, 1 (invented-metric) combining both — as data, with a P0/P1/P2 ladder. It carries NO upstream code: open-design's enforcement lives in apps/daemon/src/lint-artifact.ts (Apache-2.0) and porting it would have pulled Apache-2.0 code into an MIT script. Rules-as-data keeps the licence boundary exactly where the pack boundary already is, and the rule set reviewable without touching the gate. Its `notAdopted` list records 15 upstream rules that were deliberately refused, each with the reason and, where triage informed the call, the hit count over this pack's 67 HTML files.
usedBy: scripts/test-anti-slop-rules.mjs — fixture coverage for the rule table

subtrees.contents: evals/golden-tasks/ — tasks.json, one sample HTML fixture, 5 response fixtures
subtrees.license: MIT (repo root LICENSE, Copyright (c) 2026 xx-stack contributors)

detail.evidence: tasks.json grades this repo's own agents by name (build, plan, execution-orchestrator, design-engineer, reviewer) against this repo's paths (runtime/skills/, packs/design/evals/golden-tasks/responses/) and encodes this repo's authoring conventions. No `evals` or `golden-tasks` tree exists in any of the three upstreams at their audited heads.
Resolve paths relative to this repo's layout and implement this repo's gates; no counterpart in any audited upstream.
detail.licenceBoundary: quality-gate-html.mjs evaluates the anti-slop rules but holds none of their values — those live in craft/anti-ai-slop-rules.json, which is data derived from two Apache-2.0 upstreams. The engine's rule KINDS (gradientContainsAny, literalAny, emojiInElement, regexAny, countHexOutsideRoot, countLiteralOutsideStyle, …) were written here; no upstream code was transliterated. That is what keeps the script MIT.
detail.notWiredIntoVerify: check-craft-references.mjs and test-anti-slop-rules.mjs both run clean and exit non-zero on failure, but neither is in `npm run verify` — adding them needs a package.json edit outside the scope of the change that introduced them. A human should wire them, or decide not to.

subtrees.contents: generated index of the three subtrees
subtrees.license: MIT (repo root LICENSE) for the generated structure; the descriptions it quotes are excerpted from the vendored files and carry those files' licenses.

openQuestions.question: No subtree records the upstream commit it was vendored at. `packs/rules/manifest.json` pins ciembor/agent-rules-books at 9c87636; the design pack has no equivalent, so 'has this drifted?' can only be answered against upstream HEAD, which conflates local edits with upstream changes.

Apache-2.0 §4(b) requires modified files to carry a notice of modification. This manifest and packs/design/README.md record the modified set centrally rather than annotating each of the 40 modified files in place. Central notice is the common practice and keeps the vendored files byte-comparable against upstream, but a reviewer may prefer per-file headers. Not decided here.

design-systems/ names ~100 real brands (Apple, Stripe, BMW, Nike, Discord, ...) in headings and prose. Nominative use of a trademark to describe a design language is normally permissible, and the risk is inherited from upstream rather than created here, but nobody in this repo has made an explicit decision about it.

vendoringWindow.note: The exact vendoring commit is not recoverable, but the window is. All 57 commits in this range share one design-systems tree, and nothing in our pack distinguishes commits inside it — a single sha would be invention.
vendoringWindow.evidence: That tree is the only point in upstream history holding exactly 137 design-system slugs, and our 137 differ from it by exactly one swap: upstream's `` (absent here) replaced by `bmw-m` (traced to VoltAgent). At the same window upstream's skills/ held 52 entries and design-templates/ did not yet exist, which is why our workflow-skills sit under the older path — upstream split skills/ on 2026-05-11.
vendoringWindow.method: --filter=blob:none clone (retains every tree, so blob SHAs are readable without fetching content), git hash-object over all 304 vendored files, match-counted against every historical state of upstream's design-systems/, skills/, and design-templates/ trees.
